title: The power of Direction, Planning, and AI = Troll Valley
author: LogicalLemon-The-3rd
selftext:
This started as a proof of concept — one troll, one garden plot, six seeds, just to see if a farm loop felt like anything. It turned into a co-op farm game. Everything below is from actually shipping it, not from testing tools in isolation.

CODE. The code is written by an agent against a headless test suite, not typed by me and not accepted on vibes. Every feature lands with a test that runs the real game: farming, animals, building, saves, and co-op with multiple game instances launched as separate processes to prove player 2 can actually do the thing. That last part matters because "works on the host" is how co-op quietly breaks. I also refuse to let a build ship if the packed export is missing a file the game loads by path — the game boots the shipped pack and reports what's absent. That check has caught missing textures, missing icons, and a sound bank stripped by a build script.

ART. This is where AI lost. Characters came from Meshy and I'm fine admitting it — then they were re-rigged, retargeted and animated in Blender, because raw output doesn't fit an existing skeleton. Props, buildings and animals are all hand-modelled in Blender by the agent, driven by scripts rather than by hand. Text/image-to-3D gave me plausible-looking props with bad topology and wrong scale, and no two of them shared a style. Once I had a kit that matched, generated props were worse than the ones built to spec.

AUDIO. 208 sounds, all generated then levelled — every one normalised with a two-pass loudness pass because a single pass undershot short transients badly (a coin tick measuring −24 LUFS against a −18 target). The rule that made them feel real: no sound plays for something that did not happen. A missing sound is a silent, logged no-op, never a substitute.

WHAT I'D TELL SOMEONE STARTING. The tools are good at breadth and bad at consistency, and the failure mode is a build that looks finished and is hollow. Tests that boot the shipped artifact, not the editor, are what let me trust it.

WHAT I NEED. Testers, specifically with a second person. When a friend joins they don't drop into your farm — they load their own valley, their own cottage and animals, behind a bramble gate, and you walk between them. First three friends get a valley, up to eight trolls. That's the part nobody has hammered with a real group.

Free build, Windows, \~100 MB, unsigned so Windows will warn you: https://exmodaus.itch.io/troll-valley

Tell me what broke. Especially if you have two PCs.
